title: Monthly Wholesale Trade benchmark revision — sales, inventories and I/S ratios restated on the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey
source: EST: census.gov/wholesale/index.html announcements block, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 527,648 bytes), verbatim: "Intention to Revise - Monthly Wholesale sales, inventories, and inventories/sales ratios estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on October 26, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. EDT." Filed estimate, and doubly so: the lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and Census's own wording is "tentatively scheduled". Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the wholesale-trade-2026-12-09 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), on the same page that carries the current release. Why it earns a row rather than a footnote: it restates the ENTIRE history of the series wholesale-trade-2026-12-09 reports — level and ratio, adjusted and not — six weeks before that print delivers October data. Two concrete consequences the sweep measured. (1) Every level comparison written before 2026-10-26 breaks across it: the current published reading is June 2026, sales $794.1B (-3.0% m/m, +14.1% y/y), inventories $944.7B (+0.2% m/m, CI includes zero), I/S ratio 1.19 against 1.30 a year earlier (Census CB26-120, 2026-08-06; ratio path independently confirmed on FRED WHLSLRIRSA, 414 monthly observations 1992-01 to 2026-06). A 21-month slide from 1.33 is exactly the kind of trend a benchmark revision can flatten or deepen, so any forward test keyed to the ratio must state which basis it scores on. (2) It is not itself a GDPNow vintage — the Atlanta Fed's PostedUpdates sheet carries no 2026-10-26 row — so its effect on the nowcast arrives indirectly, through the next wholesale vintage rather than on the day. Not tradeable on its own: symbols is empty, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and a benchmark revision is a restatement of the past rather than news about the future. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
